lesson_title: The Effect of Enlargement and Reduction on Perimeter and Area
hook_text: They doubled the garden and doubled the compost. Half the patch stayed bare.
clip_script:
A community garden in Mamelodi has a square vegetable patch 5 metres on each side, fenced and covered every spring with compost at 2 bags per square metre. The committee doubles the side to 10 metres, and the treasurer doubles last year's order: 40 metres of fence and 100 bags of compost.

The fence fits exactly. The compost runs out halfway. A learner draws it on the shed wall: the new 10 by 10 patch holds four copies of the old 5 by 5. The perimeter doubled, but the area went up four times — 200 bags, not 100. Lengths scale by the factor; areas scale by its square.
visual_style: A small square garden doubles its side; a fence line stretches to twice its length while the ground splits into four tiles, and compost bags multiply on screen
call_to_action: Open the full session to predict any perimeter and area after an enlargement.
